html:
The Pijao are an Indigenous people of Colombia from the central range of the Andes, in today's Tolima and Huila, above the upper Magdalena valley.

In the 1500s and early 1600s they fought the Spanish longer and harder than almost any other people of the region. They raided Spanish towns and the roads linking Bogotá with Popayán and Quito. The Spanish governors of the New Kingdom of Granada answered with campaigns of extermination, and by the 1610s most of the Pijao had been killed, enslaved or moved. Their old neighbours to the east were the Muisca. Descendants live today in Tolima and have revived their identity, though the language is lost.
sum: The Pijao are an Indigenous people of Colombia from the central range of the Andes, in today's Tolima and Huila, above the upper Magdalena valley.
